checks: Subtracting an affine section gives an affine bijection on the hull and cancels in differences at a common real or integer base. Each sheared sampled fiber contains zero, so it lies inside its own difference body and hence inside the sampled difference hull.

Every real fiber of the sheared canonical hull lies in that common convex hull. Subtracting its two continuous points lies in twice the centrally symmetric difference hull. The reverse inclusion follows from convexity of the vertical difference section and inclusion of every sampled difference.

At each vertex of a simplex projection choose a sampled fiber point. Its unique affine interpolant belongs to the original convex set by the barycentric mixture and therefore lies in each sampled fiber. The argument also covers a singleton projection.

At the binary square all sampled bases are vertices, so the canonical hull preserves the displayed interval traces. Zero is a section and each sampled difference body is [−1,1]. The two opposite diagonal midpoint combinations give [−1,0] and [0,1] at the same real center. All generated heights are in [−1,1], so the centered fiber has precisely this interval, with difference [−2,2]. The original (3) and its calibration agree.

overlap.comparison: Studies the same two notions of difference body but uses large separated heights without a common affine section and obtains an arbitrarily large discrepancy. Its witness does not give this conditional factor two or its sharp example.

readability: The affine section is defined only on the affine span of the base, which suffices for the shear on the whole canonical hull.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: A common affine section yields the factor-two comparison under an exact shear, and the binary-square example attains the factor.
